sources.evidence: They are generally stationary, have modest capacity and may include USB communication for automatic shutdown software.

sources.why: About conventional UPS units for a NAS, not portable power stations
sources.evidence: Pick a pure sine unit with USB, confirm your NAS sees it, then pull the plug deliberately and watch it work.

sources.why: Small-rack conventional UPS picks (CyberPower, APC), not power stations
sources.evidence: Start with CyberPower CP1500PFCLCD’s current a revision for a pure-sine NAS/rack UPS.

sources.why: Names River 3 Plus / Delta 3 Plus with NUT usbhid-ups support and notes other brands lack data; no hands-on test shown
sources.evidence: A NAS and you want lithium: the EcoFlow River 3 Plus, if you can run a recent NUT release and set an on-battery shutdown timer.

missing: A checkable, hands-on shutdown test: plug a specific NAS (Synology DSM, QNAP, TrueNAS/NUT) into the RIVER 3 Plus / Delta 3 Plus by USB, confirm the NAS recognises it as a UPS, pull the plug, and show it shut down cleanly; plus current prices and which firmware/NUT versions are required, and whether any non-EcoFlow station offers the same.
why: The only major reviewer (TechRadar) is a single-product S2000 review that explicitly did not test UPS compatibility and says nothing about USB shutdown signalling. Two Anker blog pages explain the concept without naming a product. Two niche sites (racksandwatts, computingforgeeks) answer it with specs and NUT compatibility pointing at the EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus, but neither shows a verifiable shutdown test; the rest are off-target conventional-UPS pages, an affiliate listicle, or unreadable. A focused page with a tested USB shutdown on real NAS platforms, current prices and a direct pick would stand out.
